node.title: Exact-integer Johnson safe anchor for rate-half ordinary lists
node.statement: For any Reed-Solomon code, B>=1, and agreement a, put ell=B+1 and ell*a=nd+r with 0<=r<n. If n*C(d,2)+rd>C(ell,2)(k-1), then the ordinary worst list at agreement a has size at most B. The first such a is an O(log n) bigint-computable safe anchor a_IJ. At n=2^41,k=2^40 and B*=floor(q/2^128), the actual rate-half crossing lies between k+2^34 and a_IJ; a_IJ=3n/4 for B*=1,2,3 and equals floor(sqrt(n(k-1)))+1 for B*>=332114441762. No predecessor-unsafety claim is made.
